_about: Brand system for Campaign-in-a-Box. Pick one palette and one type pairing in your campaign.json. Run tools/contrast_check.py after changing any color. All fonts are free under the SIL Open Font License (Google Fonts).

river.name: River (teal and gold)
river.why: Calm, civic, outdoorsy. Reads as competent and local. Not associated with either major US party.

forest.name: Forest (green and cream)
forest.why: Rooted, steady, neighborly. Good for parks, schools, land use and rural races.

plum.name: Plum (plum and sun)
plum.why: Warm and distinctive. Stands out in a crowded field of red, white and blue signs.

contrast_pairs.use: Name and headlines on signs, mailer fronts, buttons
Slogan or office line on signs
Buttons on the website and in email

civic.name: Civic — Public Sans + Source Serif 4
civic.why: Public Sans was designed for government websites: plain, trustworthy, very legible. Source Serif adds warmth for longer reading on mailers and the website.

hyperlegible.name: Hyperlegible — Atkinson Hyperlegible
hyperlegible.why: Designed by the Braille Institute for readers with low vision. The most accessible choice; a good default if your district skews older.

condensed.name: Condensed — Barlow Condensed + Public Sans
condensed.why: A condensed headline face fits long names on a yard sign at a bigger size. Public Sans keeps body text plain.
